title: Cross-feature security review of the agent-facing surfaces
what:
One fresh review, after the slices merge, by a reviewer who is not any slice's executor. It covers:
(1) the terminal security table:
  - who may write input; cross-origin
  - tokens in a URL or env; a token used off its prefix; refusal of a door's children
  - T1a's reply_kind() allow-list: no doubled answers, no clipboard, no pixel size, only listed kinds reach the writer
  - OSC 52; links
(2) the matcher:
  - user tools shadowing names
  - exact command is not exact effect
  - origin joined by call_id (unknown never matches)
  - structural asks; door-lifetime binding; the first-answer race
  - the watcher line cap and reconnect
  - shutdown with answers in flight
(3) interplay:
  - an 'allow every term_send' rule in auto means silent shell typing; the row says so
  - yolo agents typing into terminals you opened (sudo-cached or root shells), steered by term_read text
  - guard rows against term_send (aoide words refused; ssh in a terminal is the intended path)
  - agents reading every web terminal, secrets included, which go to the provider
  - agent mail: opt-in, hourly cap, origin line, --from=minerva-agent
  - the stale aoide 0.0.25 first on PATH
(4) G1's guard file in your eidolon config dir: written 0600 and atomically; its fallback is never silent; the shared permits are not widened (a guard that compiles but lets every verdict through would be the worst case: test it)
(5) key add/remove:
  - the arm is single-use, bound to one FP, bearer-only
  - the 'FP rewritten in-origin' hole is stated in the UI
  - agents via the CLI are slowed only by G1's keys rows, and that is stated
(6) hostile remote text in cards, mesh and term_read
(7) token files on disk: 0600, rotation, stale after a crash
Findings with file:line evidence go back to the owning slice; re-review after the fixes.
tests: Review only: a written finding list with evidence.
live_check: Probes by curl against a fake perch on PORT=48137 (no browser).
